QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_3

question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (a Cat III trust-form AIF) is about to launch its third scheme under the same trust. From a legal-documentation standpoint, which of the following BEST describes the Investment Management Agreement (IMA)?

answer.text: A fresh IMA must be signed at the launch of every scheme because each scheme has a different NAV series.
The IMA is entered into between each investor and the Investment Manager, scheme by scheme.
The IMA is signed ONCE for the trust as a whole (between the Trustee on behalf of the AIF and the Investment Manager) and is not re-signed at each scheme launch.
The IMA is signed between SEBI and the Investment Manager as part of the registration process.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 228, the IMA is entered into between the Trustee on behalf of the AIF and the Investment Manager. It delegates investment-management powers to the Manager except for powers retained by the Trustee in the trust indenture, and it is signed once for the trust as a whole rather than at the launch of each scheme. The Trap: Option A confuses scheme-level PPM filings with the trust-level IMA. Option B confuses the IMA with the investor-level Contribution Agreement supported on page 229. Option D wrongly casts SEBI as a contracting party; SEBI is the regulator, not a counterparty. Note: Hold to the three source-backed facts: parties to the IMA, once-per-trust signing, and the IMA's distinction from the Contribution Agreement.
